VERDICT: FAIL
NOTES:
- Source review only; the solver was not executed. The entry point calls main(), which directly constructs homogeneous seed patterns with build_initial_patterns(); initialization uses no optimization model.
- Column generation is substantively implemented: main() solves a continuous restricted master over patterns, reads demand-constraint Pi duals, and passes them to solve_knapsack_pricing(). Pricing optimizes one roll's integer item counts under its width constraint; a valid, new pattern with dual value greater than 1 is appended to patterns and included in the next master solve.
- final_model fixes the accumulated pattern compositions and optimizes only their integer usages, so it is a permitted integer restricted master. Its positive usages supply both the reported cuts and objective_value, and json.dump(result, f, indent=2) writes them to output.json. No separate full-original-model solve appears in the supplied reachable paths.
- The explicit status requirement is violated: whenever final_model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL and SolCount > 0, main() reports status "optimal" solely from integer restricted-master optimality. There is no global optimality certificate or bound comparison, including after time-budget, iteration-limit, or other early exits from column generation. Even completed LP pricing does not alone certify the integer restricted-master incumbent globally. This reachable reporting path must use "feasible" unless global optimality is established.
